artworks.title: Menelaus Recovering Helen (Attic red-figure)
artworks.description: On this Attic red-figure crater in Munich, Menelaus finds Helen at the sack of Troy and raises his sword — then drops it as her beauty stays the blow. The vase paints the Ilioupersis reunion that ends the war he sailed to start: the Spartan husband reclaiming his wife. Staatliche Antikensammlungen, Munich.

artworks.title: Menelaus Captures Helen (Pompeii fresco)
artworks.description: A fresco from the Casa dell'Efebo at Pompeii shows Menelaus seizing Helen amid the fall of Troy — the Spartan king at the moment wrath becomes recovery. The wall-painting preserves the same night the vase-painters loved: Helen's beauty disarming the husband who came to kill her. Pompeii.

artworks.title: Menelaus Holding the Body of Patroclus
artworks.description: This view of the Pasquino Group type shows a helmeted warrior supporting a naked dead companion — long identified as Menelaus retrieving Patroclus' corpse from Iliad 17. Whether read as Menelaus–Patroclus or Ajax–Achilles, the group entered Menelaus' visual afterlife as the Spartan king's aristeia over his fallen comrade. Marble group type (Loggia dei Lanzi and related copies).

artworks.title: Paris and Helen Surprised by Menelaus
artworks.description: Gelton stages the casus belli as a bedroom shock: Menelaus bursts in on Paris and Helen, the wronged husband interrupting the elopement that will launch a thousand ships. The Danish canvas keeps Menelaus as the war's personal spark — Sparta's king before the walls of Troy. Oil on canvas, Statens Museum for Kunst, Copenhagen.

artworks.title: Helen Offering Menelaus the Potion of Queen Polydamna
artworks.description: Vouet paints the Odyssey's Spartan hall: Helen mixes the Egyptian nepenthe for Menelaus and their guests so grief for Troy will lift. The canvas shows the king home at last — the husband who wandered through Egypt and now entertains Telemachus with Helen beside him. Oil on canvas.

films.title: Troy
films.description: Brendan Gleeson's Menelaus is the wronged husband who sails for Helen and dies early in Petersen's rewrite — Sparta's king reduced to the spark that lights the war.

films.title: Helen of Troy
films.description: Wise's epic keeps Menelaus as the Spartan husband robbed of Helen — the casus belli in CinemaScope, before the walls and the horse.

films.title: Troy: Fall of a City
films.description: The BBC/Netflix cycle gives Menelaus the long war for his wife — less Homeric host than a husband who will not let the insult stand.

films.title: The Odyssey
films.description: Konchalovsky's miniseries keeps the Telemachy stop in Sparta: Menelaus and Helen, home at last, telling Telemachus what they know of Odysseus.

music.title: La belle Hélène
music.description: Offenbach's opéra bouffe makes Menelaus the comic cuckold of the Second Empire — the Spartan king as the joke the gods and Paris are in on.
